solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Station messenger boy gets deduction from wages?

parts.note: a stop is a station where a bus or train halts
a page is a boy who carries messages, as in a hotel

explanation.surface: A railway station's errand boy finds money docked from his pay.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that the definition is playful: a stoppage is money stopped out of pay.
explanation.definitionFit: A stoppage is a sum withheld from pay, such as tax or a fine, so it is a deduction.

clue.text: Unclear total for Chinese food

parts.note: dim means faint or unclear
a sum is a total

explanation.surface: A vague bill at a Chinese restaurant.
explanation.definitionFit: Dim sum are small Cantonese dumplings and snacks, a classic kind of Chinese cuisine.

clue.text: Only fish

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both single or only, and a flat seafish served as Dover sole.

clue.text: Conceal lofty-sounding camp greeting

parts.note: to hide is to conceal

indicators.note: sounding asks for the word for lofty as it is spoken, giving letters that sound the same

parts.note: lofty means high

explanation.surface: Hide a greeting that sounds rather grand at a holiday camp.
explanation.walkthrough: Hi-de-Hi! was a British TV sitcom set in a 1950s holiday camp, its title the staff's cheery greeting to campers.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase was the catchphrase greeting called out by entertainers at the sitcom's holiday camp.

clue.text: Second to none, unlike the House of Lords?

definitions.meaning: the Lords is full of peers, so something unlike it is without peers

explanation.walkthrough: The second definition is whimsical: the House of Lords is made up of peers, so the opposite would have none.
explanation.definitionFit: Without equal means having no peers, i.e. matchless; the Lords pun reads it literally as lacking noblemen.

clue.text: Posers seldom troubled

indicators.note: troubled means disturbed, so the letters of seldom are stirred into a new order

explanation.surface: People who strike poses are rarely bothered.
explanation.definitionFit: Artists' or fashion models pose for a camera or painter, so they are posers in the literal sense.

clue.text: Study onset of tropical depression

parts.note: a den is a private room or study

indicators.note: the onset of a word is its beginning, so take its first letter

explanation.surface: Researching the start of a tropical weather low.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface makes 'depression' meteorological; here it is a hollow.
explanation.definitionFit: A dent is a small hollow pressed into a surface, which is a physical depression.

clue.text: Fresh oil needed on journey in African capital

parts.note: a trip is a journey

indicators.note: fresh means new, so the letters of oil are made into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Topping up with new oil on a trip to a city in Africa.
explanation.definitionFit: Tripoli is the capital city of Libya in North Africa.

clue.text: Distant Head going off to show feeling

indicators.note: the head of the word departs, so its first letter is removed

parts.note: remote means distant

explanation.surface: An aloof headteacher leaving shows emotion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Head' looks like a person; it is the first letter of REMOTE, which goes off to leave EMOTE.
explanation.definitionFit: To emote is to express emotion openly, often theatrically, so it means to display feeling.

clue.text: Stick with former head of economics

parts.note: past means former, as in past president

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: Staying loyal to an ex-chair of the economics department.
explanation.definitionFit: Paste is glue, and as a verb to paste is to stick something down.

clue.text: Serious fellow heard

indicators.note: heard means the name is taken as it sounds when spoken

parts.note: Ernest is a man's name, standing for any fellow

explanation.surface: A grave man gets listened to.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface recalls Wilde's play The Importance of Being Earnest, which turns on the same pun.
explanation.definitionFit: Earnest means sincere and grave in intention, which is a synonym of serious.

clue.text: It's a crime breaking a truce

indicators.note: breaking smashes up the letters of the phrase so they can be rebuilt

explanation.surface: Violating a ceasefire is criminal.
explanation.definitionFit: An armistice is a formal agreement to stop fighting, which is a truce.

clue.text: Sailor with a method to keep secret

parts.note: an old salt is a seasoned sailor
a way is a method

explanation.surface: A seaman with a technique for keeping things quiet.
explanation.definitionFit: To salt away is an idiom for hiding money or goods for later, keeping a hoard secret.

clue.text: Cutting tool used to be returned

indicators.note: returned sends the word back the way it came, so it is read backwards

parts.note: was is a past form of the verb to be, as in used to be

explanation.surface: A blade borrowed earlier must be given back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'used to be' is split: 'used' supplies WAS while 'to be returned' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: A saw is a toothed blade for cutting wood or metal, a classic cutting tool.

clue.text: Scottish churchgoers: we're very cold when speaking

indicators.note: when speaking means the words are taken as they sound aloud

parts.note: if we're very cold, we freeze

explanation.surface: Scottish worshippers complain about the chilly kirk.
explanation.walkthrough: The Wee Frees is the nickname of the Free Church of Scotland, a strict Presbyterian body.
explanation.definitionFit: The nickname refers to members of the small Free Church of Scotland, so they are Scottish worshippers.

clue.text: Wood seen in backing Daimler

indicators.note: backing means the letters are read in reverse
seen in says the letters sit inside the car's name

explanation.surface: Timber trim spotted in a reversing Daimler car.
explanation.definitionFit: Elm is a tree and its timber, so it is a kind of wood.

clue.text: Dynamo working twenty-four hours

indicators.note: working means operating or in motion, so the letters are set moving into a new order

explanation.surface: A generator running round the clock.
explanation.definitionFit: Monday is a day of the week, and a day is a period of twenty-four hours.

clue.text: Member is behind what parliaments can do

parts.note: a leg is a member, i.e. a limb
late means behind schedule

explanation.surface: An MP is running late with the business of parliament.
explanation.definitionFit: To legislate is to make laws, which is the chief power held by a parliament.

clue.text: Biker initially leaves rubbish in this part of house?

indicators.note: leaves means that letter departs from the word for rubbish

parts.note: garbage is rubbish

indicators.note: initially means take the first letter of the word

explanation.surface: A motorcyclist dumps his junk in a room of the home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'this' points back to the clue's scene: the place a biker leaves rubbish.
explanation.definitionFit: A garage is a building or room attached to a house for keeping a car or motorbike.

clue.text: Trouble with lapse showing up a handsome young man

parts.note: ado means fuss or trouble

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word is written from the bottom, so it is read backwards

parts.note: a sin is a moral lapse

explanation.surface: A good-looking youth reveals his troubles and failings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'showing up' looks like 'appearing', but in a down entry it reverses the lapse only, not the trouble.
explanation.definitionFit: Adonis was the beautiful youth loved by Aphrodite in Greek myth, so the name stands for any handsome young man.

clue.text: Ruffian spoiled travelling attraction

indicators.note: spoiled means ruined, so the letters of the thug are wrecked and reassembled

explanation.surface: A thug ruined the visiting fairground.
explanation.definitionFit: A funfair is an entertainment of rides and stalls that moves from town to town, a travelling amusement.

clue.text: Handled soft material

definitions.meaning: touched with the hands, the past tense of feel
a fabric of matted wool or fibres

explanation.definitionFit: The word is the past tense of feel, i.e. touched, and also a matted woollen fabric.

clue.text: The morning belonging to us for an affair

parts.note: a.m. is short for the morning hours
our means belonging to us

explanation.surface: Our morning is reserved for a romantic liaison.
explanation.definitionFit: Borrowed from French, the word means a love affair, often a secret one.

clue.text: Regrettably, a girl is cut short

indicators.note: cut short means the word loses its last letter

parts.note: a lass is a girl

explanation.surface: Sadly, a young woman's career ends early.
explanation.definitionFit: Alas is an exclamation of sorrow, used in the sense of unfortunately or sadly.

clue.text: Transport animal a shopping centre returned

indicators.note: returned means the letters are brought back in reverse order

parts.note: a mall is a shopping centre

explanation.surface: A pack beast that was returned to the mall.
explanation.definitionFit: The llama is a South American camelid used as a pack animal for carrying loads.

clue.text: Rock played in Tangier

indicators.note: played means performed in a new way, so the letters of the city are rearranged

explanation.surface: Rock music performed in a Moroccan port.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rock' suggests music; here it is stone.
explanation.definitionFit: Granite is a hard igneous stone, so it is a type of rock.
